Monica / Jonas —

Monitoring picked up a sharp P99 latency jump beginning ~09:06 PT for the finlytics-prod tenant. P90 is unaffected, but P99 moved from ~420ms to ~3.8s and a handful of requests returned 504s. Early signs point at KV cache churn + longer model attention windows in a small subset of requests.

I've attached a quick screenshot from the dashboard and the raw alert. I’ve already throttled the suspect routing policy for a single pool to avoid wider impact. Can we decide on an immediate mitigation (circuit breaker / model variant fallback) and what customer note we should send?

Proposed immediate actions:
- Jonas/Hannah: consider a temporary circuit breaker on requests > 8s and route affected traffic to model-quant-1 (lower-cost variant) for 20m window.
- Marissa/Dylan: prepare a short customer note (1-2 bullets) explaining we saw a P99 spike, immediate mitigation applied, ask for permission to enable fallback for next 30 minutes while we observe.
- If customer refuses, we offer a scheduled rolling rollback to the prior model snapshot (less ideal during their batch).

Can each of you reply with quick ack + your preference? I’ll draft the customer note once we have alignment.

Hi Sanjay —
Quick update from our side: we observed a short-lived spike in tail latency this morning that affected some of your batch jobs. Our SRE team has applied a limited throttle to the most impacted routing pool to reduce failed requests. To stabilize throughput while we investigate, we recommend — with your approval — enabling a short automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (model-quant-1) for 30 minutes.

Why this helps: the fallback reduces memory and KV pressure on the pool and keeps most requests within target latency. If you’d rather not enable fallback, we can perform a controlled rollback to the previous model snapshot; that will require a short maintenance window.

Please reply with a one-word confirmation ("enable" or "rollback") and we’ll act immediately. If we don’t hear back in 10 minutes we will hold and continue monitoring.
